implementation_summary: Added detectTechnology(pages: RawPage[], headers?: ResponseHeaders): TechnologyResult. It uses a fixed signature table typed Record<TechnologyName, Signature[]>, so leaving out any of the 21 TECHNOLOGIES is a compile error. There are six kinds of signature: meta generator regex, script/stylesheet path substring, script/stylesheet host (exact or sub-domain), in-page marker from RawPage.frameworkMarkers (case-insensitive), response header (present, optionally with a value regex), and the host the page itself is served from. Evidence uses fixed wording ('meta generator', 'stylesheet from /wp-content/', 'script from cdn.shopify.com', 'page marker __NEXT_DATA__', 'x-powered-by header', 'site address on blogspot.com'). Results are collected across all pages; the headers argument is merged with each page's responseHeaders and header names are lower-cased. Technologies come out in TECHNOLOGIES order, each once, and each evidence string appears once. When nothing matches the result is {status:'not-identified'}, so an 'identified' result never has an empty list. Pure: the only imports are @qa/types and ./raw-page.js.

risks: Marker names must line up with what BE-301 readPage puts in frameworkMarkers. The table expects these exact names (matched case-insensitively): __NEXT_DATA__, next-route-announcer, ng-version, astro-island, data-wf-site, data-wf-page, data-reactroot, _reactRootContainer, __reactContainer, __NUXT__, __NUXT_DATA__, data-v-app, data-server-rendered, ___gatsby, data-drupal-selector.
The signatures for Zoho Sites, Dukaan and GoDaddy (hosts and generator wording) are best-effort and have not been checked against live sites.
No technology implies another: Gatsby or Next.js does not add React unless a React signature is also seen.
Headers are matched by their names only, and no header value is copied into the evidence.
handoff: Import detectTechnology and the ResponseHeaders type from packages/core/src/audit/analysis/technology.ts. Pass every recorded RawPage. The optional second argument takes extra response headers (for example the start page's, lower-case names preferred) and is merged with each page's own responseHeaders. BE-301 must report the in-page markers under the exact names listed in risks.
